inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0 <= lambda < p.

n=lambda+1>0, I has n elements, dim_C V=n, and (e_i)_{i in I} is a complex basis of V, with e_0=v. For every integer t>=0, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. All y^t v vanish for t>lambda. The matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. For every i in I and r>=0, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r<=i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power coefficients are integers.

Multiplication R tensor_Z M -> V, s tensor m -> s m, is injective with image M_R. M_R is free over R of rank n and spans V over C. Every X_r and Y_r (r>=0) preserves M and M_R; x,y,h preserve M and M_R, so their reductions are defined. For all i,j in I, Pi=E_{lambda,lambda}, X_{lambda-i} Pi=E_{i,lambda}, Pi Y_{lambda-j}=binom(lambda,j) E_{lambda,j}, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R, and E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_{lambda-i} Pi Y_{lambda-j}. Consequently every E_ij preserves M_R.
The multiplication map Q tensor_R J -> C, q tensor c -> q c, is injective, and dim_Q(Q tensor_R J)=1. There exists b in J with b!=0, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} an R-basis of M_R.

There are natural K-linear isomorphisms V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/p M_R) tensor_{F_p} K, with first map m tensor c -> m tensor c and its inverse (s m) tensor c -> m tensor (bar(s)c), for s in R, where bar is the stated ring map, and second map z tensor c -> [z] tensor c. For some nonzero b in J with J=R b and (b e_i) an R-basis of M_R the images beta_i of b e_i give a K-basis of V(K) indexed by I, so dim_K V(K)=n>0. Relative to this basis the induced generators have matrices red(x) beta_0=0, red(x) beta_i=(lambda-i+1) beta_{i-1} for i>=1, red(y) beta_i=(i+1) beta_{i+1} for i<lambda, red(y) beta_lambda=0, red(h) beta_i=(lambda-2i) beta_i, with integer coefficients interpreted in K. argument.text: Choose b0 as in N004. For every denominator d not divisible by p, its image in K is nonzero, since H001 gives characteristic p; it is therefore invertible. Define rho(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Cross multiplication in Q proves independence of the chosen fraction, since denominators remain invertible; it also proves additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of 1. This is the ring map R -> K. Define V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c -> m tensor c. Its inverse sends (r m) tensor c to m tensor rho(r)c and extends over finite sums; equivalently on R tensor_Z M it sends (r tensor m) tensor c to m tensor rho(r)c using N002. The Z- and R-balancing relations prove both maps well-defined, and on pure tensors their composites are identity; pure tensors span, so these are inverse K-linear maps. Since rho(p)=0, the map z tensor c -> [z] tensor c takes M_R tensor_R K to (M_R/p M_R) tensor_{F_p} K. Its inverse sends [z] tensor c to z tensor c: changing z by p z' adds z' tensor pc=0, and scalar balancing is precisely reduction of rho modulo p. Every residue class in R/pR is the residue of an integer: choose an inverse of its denominator modulo the prime p. Its kernel is pR, so R/pR=F_p canonically and the displayed F_p scalar structure is valid. These checks prove the second pair of maps well-defined and inverse.

produces.statement: rho:R -> K is a unital ring map sending a/d to bar(a)/bar(d) for integers a,d with p not dividing d. There are inverse K-linear maps V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K, m tensor c -> m tensor c, and (s m) tensor c -> m tensor rho(s)c, extended over finite sums. There are inverse K-linear maps M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/p M_R) tensor_{F_p} K, z tensor c -> [z] tensor c, and [z] tensor c -> z tensor c. Here R/pR is identified with F_p by integer reduction.

argument.text: Define beta_i in V(K) by transporting (b0 e_i) tensor 1 through the first isomorphism of F001. Apply M001 to the R-basis (b0 e_i) of M_R from N004 and the R-algebra K defined by rho. It says 1 tensor (b0 e_i) is a K-basis of K tensor_R M_R; exchanging the tensor factors sends it to (b0 e_i) tensor 1, with inverse the same exchange. Thus beta is a K-basis of V(K). The same coordinate argument over R/pR shows the images of b0 e_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/p M_R: an element of M_R lies in p M_R exactly when every R-coordinate is in pR. Apply M004 over K to beta and use N001 to obtain dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0. N001 gives the x,y,h matrices and the X_r,Y_r matrices on e, and N002 gives preservation of M and M_R by every one of these operators. Multiplication by the scalar b0 commutes with all these complex-linear operators; restriction to M_R and then the tensor maps in F001 therefore give on beta precisely those matrices with their integer entries mapped into K. The tensor maps intertwine the operators because this holds on m tensor c and extends linearly.

produces.statement: beta is a K-basis of V(K) and dim_K V(K)=n>0. beta_i maps to (b0 e_i) tensor 1 under V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K. The matrices on beta, with all integer coefficients mapped into K, are red(x)beta_0=0, red(x)beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, red(y)beta_i=(i+1)beta_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, red(y)beta_lambda=0, and red(h)beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. For i in I and r>=0, red(X_r)beta_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)beta_{i-r} if r<=i and zero otherwise; red(Y_r)beta_i=binom(i+r,r)beta_{i+r} if i+r<=lambda and zero otherwise.

argument.text: For 0<=r<=lambda<p, every factor from 1 through r has nonzero image in K, so r! is nonzero. The operator equality r! X_r=x^r on M is an equality of integer-linear maps because X_r preserves M by N002; tensoring it gives red(X_r)=(r!)^(-1)red(x)^r, and likewise for Y. Formula N002 for E_ij is an identity of R-linear operators on M_R, not necessarily integer operators on M; tensor it on M_R and use F001 and F002. By its matrix on b0 e_k its left side becomes the K-matrix unit F_ij of beta. Its right side becomes binom(lambda,j)^(-1) red(X_{lambda-i}) red(Y_lambda) red(X_lambda) red(Y_{lambda-j}). The image of binom(lambda,j) is nonzero: it was a unit in R by N002, and a unital ring map to a field sends a unit to a unit. All divided-power indices in this expression are between 0 and lambda. Fix any K-subspace W0 and assume L1: it is invariant under red(x),red(y). Iteration gives invariance under their powers, and K-linearity of W0 gives invariance under scalar multiples and compositions, so W0 is invariant under every F_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W0. This proves all the asserted reduction statements, with b=b0.
